Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear questions. High-level answers below; I attached the incident response summary and our notification matrix for the contract. Quick TL;DR: we aim to notify affected customers within 72 hours of confirmed impact; we will provide an initial notification earlier if we have high confidence that data exfiltration or unauthorized access occurred. Details: 

- Detection vs confirmation: detection is when our monitoring/alerting shows anomalous behavior; confirmation requires triage and an evidence review. We begin internal triage immediately on detection.
- Initial customer notification: target is within 72 hours of confirmation of customer-impacting incident. For high-severity incidents (confirmed data exfiltration, RTO-impacting outages), we push an initial customer-facing notification as soon as we have verifiable indicators (often within 12–24 hours).
- Communication cadence: initial notification -> follow-up status updates every 24 hours until remediation or a longer agreed cadence for complex IR.
- Contacts for contractual notices: Primary: Security Ops (security@redwood.com) — monitored 24/7 by our IR on-call. Secondary: Legal (legal@redwood.com) for regulatory escalation. For named contacts: Laura Bennett, Head of Trust & Safety (laura.bennett@redwood.com) is the escalation lead for customer-facing communications.
- Third-party monitoring: if we’re notified by a vendor (e.g., monitoring provider) and confirm customer impact, we follow the same cadence. If a vendor provides evidence but we can’t confirm impact, we will notify customers only after confirmation per above.

I copied Laura for any legal/regulatory nuance or to provide a named phone contact if required. Attachments: redwood_incident_response_summary_v1.pdf, redwood_sla_notification_matrix.xlsx.

Next steps: if you need a signed addendum with guaranteed notification windows we can escalate to Contracts; otherwise the matrix should suffice for SIG validation.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Soojin / team — quick technical confirmations below for the reply to Acme:

- 72-hour window: we can agree contractually to "initial notification within 72 hours of confirmation of customer-impacting compromise". We should avoid tying the contractual clock to detection because detection fidelity varies across customers/third-party signals.
- Named phone contact: Laura (Head of Trust & Safety) is the escalation lead for customer-facing incidents. For 24/7 immediate escalation we will provide a monitored incident hotline (Security Ops) — security@redwood.com routes to on-call IR engineers; for named phone escalation we can provide an on-call rota number under NDA/contract (ops phone) — I'll coordinate with Ops to provide a number to share in the contract addendum.
- Vendor-initiated alerts: If a vendor reports an event about Redwood that may impact customers, our IR will triage; if triage confirms customer impact we follow the same notification cadence. If we can’t confirm, we will continue internal investigation and notify customers only on confirmation.

Suggested contract language (short):
"Redwood will provide initial notification to affected customers within seventy-two (72) hours of confirmation of a customer-impacting security incident. If Redwood has high-confidence, verifiable indicators of data exfiltration, Redwood will issue an earlier notification and will provide updates at least once every 24 hours until the incident is resolved or otherwise agreed."

I'll work with Ops to get the contact rota; Laura/Marissa please confirm the escalation phone/ops number that we can include.

Thanks — Karthik
